solution: Here \(|\vec a_k|^2=\tan^2\theta_k+1=\sec^2\theta_k\) and \(|\vec b_k|^2=1+\cot^2\theta_k=\csc^2\theta_k\). With \(\theta_k=\dfrac{2^{k-1}\pi}{2^n+1}\), the doubling of angles satisfies \(2^n\theta=\pi-\theta\), and telescoping the two sums under this symmetry gives \(\dfrac{\sum_{k=1}^{n}|\vec a_k|^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{n}|\vec b_k|^2}=3\).

solution: \(P(3, - 1,2)\) \[Q(1,2, - 4)\] \[\overrightarrow{PR} \parallel 4\widehat{i} - \widehat{j} + 2\widehat{k}\] \[\overrightarrow{QS} \parallel - 2\widehat{i} + \widehat{j} - 2\widehat{k}\] \(dr\) 's of normal to the plane containing \(P,T\& Q\) will be proportional to : \[\left| \begin{matrix} \widehat{i} & \widehat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 4 & - 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 1 & - 2 \end{matrix} \right|\] \[\therefore\ \frac{\mathcal{l}}{0} = \frac{m}{4} = \frac{n}{2}\] For point, \(T:\overrightarrow{PT} = \frac{x - 3}{4} = \frac{y + 1}{- 1} = \frac{z - 2}{2} = \lambda\) \[\overrightarrow{QT} = \frac{x - 1}{- 2} = \frac{y - 1}{1} = \frac{z + 4}{- 2} = \mu\] \[T:(4\lambda + 3, - \lambda - 1,2\lambda + 2)\] \[\cong (2\mu + 1,\mu + 2, - 2\mu - 4)\] \[4\lambda + 3 = - 2\mu + 1 \Rightarrow 2\lambda + \mu = - 1\] \[\lambda + \mu = - 3 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2\] & \(\mu = - 5\ \lambda + \mu = - 3 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2\) So point \(T:(11, - 3,6)\) \[\overrightarrow{OA} = (11\widehat{i} - 3\widehat{j} + 6\widehat{k}) \pm \left( \frac{2\widehat{j} + \widehat{k}}{\sqrt{5}} \right)\sqrt{5}\] \[\overrightarrow{OA} = (11\widehat{i} - 3\widehat{j} + 6\widehat{k}) \pm (2\widehat{j} + \widehat{k})\] \[\overrightarrow{OA} = 11\widehat{i} - \widehat{j} + 7\widehat{k}\] or \[11\widehat{i} - 5\widehat{j} + 5\widehat{k}\] \[|\overrightarrow{OA}| = \sqrt{121 + 1 + 49} = \sqrt{171}\] or \[\sqrt{121 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{171}\]

solution: We know that \[\begin{matrix} & O\text{~(orthocentre)~}\frac{\overrightarrow{p} + \overrightarrow{q} + \overrightarrow{r}}{4} \\ & C\text{~(circum centre)~}\alpha\overrightarrow{p} + \beta\overrightarrow{q} + \gamma\overrightarrow{r} \end{matrix}\] \[C(\text{~centroid~}) = \frac{\overrightarrow{p} + \overrightarrow{q} + \overrightarrow{r}}{3}\] by relation \[\begin{matrix} & \Rightarrow 2(\alpha\overrightarrow{p} + \beta\overrightarrow{q} + \gamma\overrightarrow{r}) + \frac{\overrightarrow{p} + \overrightarrow{q} + \overrightarrow{r}}{4} = 3\left( \frac{\overrightarrow{p} + \overrightarrow{q} + \overrightarrow{r}}{3} \right) \\ & \ \Rightarrow 8(\alpha\overrightarrow{p} + \beta\overrightarrow{q} + \gamma\overrightarrow{r}) = 3(\overrightarrow{p} + \overrightarrow{q} + \overrightarrow{r}) \\ & \ \Rightarrow 8\alpha = 3,8\beta = 3,8\gamma = 3 \\ & \alpha = \frac{3}{8},\beta = \frac{3}{8},\gamma = \frac{3}{8} \\ & \ \therefore\alpha + 2\beta + 5\gamma \\ & \frac{3}{8} + \frac{6}{8} + \frac{15}{8} = \frac{24}{8} = 3 \end{matrix}\]
note: wrote alpha + 2 beta + 3 gamma; the question asks alpha + 2 beta + 5 gamma (the sum shown, 3/8 + 6/8 + 15/8, is the 5 gamma one). Key A unchanged.
